subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

items.prompt: What two factors determine the change in an object's motion?
items.answer: The net force on it and its mass

steps: Newton's Second Law relates force, mass, and motion.

items.prompt: What is the net force on an object?
items.answer: The sum of all forces acting on it

steps: Add forces (with direction) to get the net force.

items.prompt: If the net force is zero, what happens to an object's motion?

steps: Balanced forces mean no change in motion.

items.prompt: Two carts get the same push; one is heavier. Which speeds up more?

steps: Less mass means more acceleration for the same force.

items.prompt: A box has a 10 N force left and a 10 N force right. What is the net force?
A box has a 10 N force right and a 4 N force left. What is the net force?

steps: 10 N - 4 N = 6 N in the direction of the larger force.

items.prompt: If you increase the force on a cart but keep its mass the same, acceleration will:
If you increase an object's mass but keep the force the same, acceleration will:

steps: More mass is harder to accelerate.

items.prompt: Why is it harder to speed up a loaded truck than an empty one with the same engine force?
items.answer: The loaded truck has more mass, so the same force changes its motion less

steps: More mass resists changes in motion.

items.prompt: A ball rolls at a steady speed in a straight line with no net force. What can you say about the forces on it?
items.answer: They are balanced (net force is zero)

items.prompt: What two things determine the change in an object's motion?
items.answer: The net force and the mass
